tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand why lpc-toolkit separates LPC sprite composition from its user interfaces. It establishes the monorepo boundaries, the working core and web packages, the planned CLI, and the mandatory attribution and environment-agnostic design constraints that shape every later step.

tour.title: Core Public API
tour.description: The core barrel is the most widely referenced node in the graph and defines the supported surface shared by browser and future Node callers. Read it alongside the API guide to see how catalog loading, composition, recoloring, hashes, results, and credits are intentionally exposed without leaking implementation details.
tour.languageLesson: A TypeScript barrel re-exports selected symbols from multiple modules, giving consumers one stable import path while allowing the implementation to remain split into focused files.

tour.title: Portable Core Contracts
tour.description: The shared types define the vocabulary for sheets, selections, frames, palettes, composition output, and credit metadata introduced by the public API. Adapter interfaces invert control over canvas creation and image loading, which is the key decision that keeps the core independent of both DOM and Node filesystem APIs.
tour.languageLesson: Dependency inversion in TypeScript is commonly expressed with interfaces: the core depends on a capability contract, while each runtime supplies the concrete implementation.

tour.title: Catalog and Frames
tour.description: Building on those contracts, catalog loading turns LPC definitions into searchable, composable sheet data. Frame and animation helpers then map that data onto the canonical spritesheet geometry, giving composition code a consistent model for selecting animation rows and output frames.

tour.title: Composition Pipeline
tour.description: The composition module is a broad orchestration hub: it resolves selected layers, applies frame and recolor rules, draws through the injected adapter, and returns structured output. Credits and asset validation are coupled to this flow so every successful render carries attribution derived from the same assets that produced its pixels.

tour.title: React Boot Sequence
tour.description: The Vite entry point mounts the React application under StrictMode, while App owns startup concerns such as loading assets and palettes and restoring URL state. This is where the environment-neutral engine from the previous steps becomes a concrete browser application without moving browser dependencies into the core package.
tour.languageLesson: React StrictMode deliberately re-runs selected development-time lifecycles to reveal unsafe side effects, so initialization code should be repeatable and cleanup-aware.

tour.title: Selection State Model
tour.description: The selection reducer is the main application-state hub, translating editor actions into the core model consumed by composition. Catalog-tree, filtering, and localization helpers derive stable UI choices from that state, keeping presentation concerns separate from the pure sprite engine.
tour.languageLesson: Reducer state transitions are pure functions of the previous state and an action, which makes complex editor behavior easier to test and replay than scattered component mutations.

tour.title: Editor Workspace
tour.description: The layer-stack harness coordinates the visible character-building workflow: composition previews, responsive regions, layer controls, search, filters, popovers, and status feedback. Its child components turn the reducer and catalog behavior from Step 7 into an interactive desktop and mobile editor while leaving pixel processing in the core.

tour.title: Browser Assets and Export
tour.description: Browser adapters satisfy the core canvas and image-loading contracts using packaged ZIP assets, including caching and bounded loading behavior. Export helpers then encode composed frames and package animation-grouped PNGs together with attribution metadata, completing the browser path from asset source to downloadable result.

tour.title: Build and Quality Gates
tour.description: Asset-release and copy scripts prepare the migrated LPC data consumed by the web runtime, making asset generation part of the build rather than hidden application behavior. Workspace configuration, focused composition tests, and the GitHub Actions pipeline enforce the TypeScript, test, and packaging contracts across the monorepo before deployment.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows organize independent checks as jobs and sequential commands as steps; keeping asset preparation explicit makes CI reproduce the same inputs used by local builds.
